overview: Chemists study substances and how they react. They analyze compounds, develop new products and formulas, and test materials for quality and safety in fields such as pharmaceuticals, food, plastics and energy. O*NET rates knowledge of chemistry at 4.92 out of 5 for this job and science at 4.12. A bachelor's degree is enough for many lab jobs, held by 56% in O*NET data, while 30% hold a doctoral degree for research roles. The BLS May 2025 median is $91,240 across 82,770 jobs. Lab work involves tight deadlines and hazardous materials, with strict safety rules.
pay: Chemists earn a median of $91,240, and the top 10% earn $160,830 or more, often with a PhD in industry. The District of Columbia has the highest state median at $149,860, 64% above the national figure, followed by Maryland and Delaware. California has the most chemists, 9,820.

faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $91,240 a year. The lowest 10% earn under $58,460 and the top 10% earn $160,830 or more. The District of Columbia, Maryland ($140,670) and Delaware ($129,860) pay the most, while Maine and Montana have the lowest state medians.

faq.q: What degree do you need to be a chemist?
faq.a: A bachelor's degree in chemistry is the minimum for most jobs, and O*NET places the job in Job Zone 4. In O*NET data, 56% of chemists hold a bachelor's degree, 10% a master's and 30% a doctoral degree. There are 12 related majors, including analytical and organic chemistry.

faq.q: What does a chemist do every day?
faq.a: Most chemists run experiments, analyze samples with lab instruments and write up results. Others develop new products or check quality in manufacturing. O*NET rates critical thinking and reading comprehension at 4 out of 5 and writing at 3.75, since reports are part of the job.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to chemist?
faq.a: The closest moves are Food Scientists and Technologists (81% match), Chemical Engineers (80%) and Microbiologists (80%), based on O*NET 31.0. Chemical Engineers earn $125,040, 37% more than chemists, and Biochemists and Biophysicists earn $127,410, 40% more, according to BLS May 2025.
